Aggressive reduction of the gate length has been essential in this progress and gate-lengths have already been realized experimentally in 20 nm scale in a previous ESA project (ref. no. T106-603EF). Availability of low-noise amplifiers (LNA) at sub-mm wave frequencies and above 600 GHz is needed for future space-borne radiometers for Earth observation for three reasons: Firstly, employment of a low-noise pre-amplifier in front of a Schottky mixer allows improvement in receiver sensitivity. This can facilitate multipixel heterodyne instruments based on microwave photonics downconverter and centralized photonics LO. Thirdly, LNAs make direct-detection radiometers possible, allowing significant simplification of the receiver architecture, as nolocal oscillator will be needed. At system level, in complex heterodyne instruments, the LNA also helps in reducing backward leakage of the local oscillator signal, therefore improving system auto-compatibility. This activity aims at pushing the LNA technology towards THz regime based on the emerging state-of-the-art technologies and design skills. LNA demonstrators in this activity are designed, manufactured and tested at two dedicated frequencies in the vicinity of 1 THz.
